notice: Information only, not investment advice. Sector claims below are the Ethiopian Investment Commission's (EIC) own promotional statements from pages that carry a 2023 copyright; figures are EIC's, are not independently audited, and several refer to 2019–2022. Where this dashboard holds its own data, it is cross-linked so you can compare. Always verify with the issuing body and take professional legal and financial advice.

sectors.name: Agriculture
sectors.tagline: A large domestic food market plus export access (coffee, oilseeds, fruit and vegetables, cut flowers).

claims.t: Ethiopia is the third-largest producer of wheat in Africa and fifth-largest of tropical fruits (EIC).
74.3 million hectares are described as suitable for agriculture, across 18 agro-ecological zones (EIC).
Third-largest producer of Arabica coffee, citing USDA; top non-EU exporter of cut flowers to the EU (EIC).
Cereals market value estimated at over US$4.1 billion (EIC).

foreign.note: EIC invites foreign investors but does not list the restrictions on this page. Check the investment regulation (links below) for the current rules on agricultural land and activities.

sectors.name: Agro-processing
sectors.tagline: Replace imported processed food and reach regional and export markets.

claims.t: Imports of processed agricultural products reached US$4.7 billion (EIC).
Main imports named: edible oil, refined sugar, malt barley, processed fruit, pasta and macaroni, milled rice (EIC).
Three integrated agro-industrial parks exist: Burie (Amhara), Yirgalem (Sidama) and Bulbula (Oromia) (EIC).

foreign.note: Manufacturing is the sector EIC says received over half of FDI inflows. Confirm current incentives for your activity with EIC.

claims.t: The sector is said to have grown four-fold since 2020, generating over US$140 million in exports (EIC).
Brands listed as producing in Ethiopia include PVH, H&M, The Children's Place and Decathlon (EIC).
EIC states a goal of US$30 billion in exports over the next decade.
EIC credits AGOA and EBA trade preferences. Check current eligibility: US AGOA benefits for Ethiopia were reported withdrawn from January 2022 (dashboard note, not verified here).

foreign.note: EIC says investment-law reforms cleared the way for integrated textile industries.

sectors.name: Leather & leather products
sectors.tagline: A very large livestock base feeding tanning, footwear and leather goods.

claims.t: Livestock population described as nearly 200 million, the largest in Africa (EIC).
Footwear, gloves, bags and garments are said to generate over US$120 million a year (EIC).
Capacity to produce over 500 million square feet of finished leather a year; target of 300,000 jobs by 2030 (EIC).

foreign.note: Confirm current rules and incentives with EIC.

sectors.name: Pharmaceuticals
sectors.tagline: Local production to replace imports in a fast-growing market.

claims.t: Domestic pharmaceutical market estimated at US$1 billion, with 85% of supply imported (EIC, citing a 2019 Frost & Sullivan / World Bank presentation).
Demand said to be growing about 15% a year, projected at US$1.8 billion in 2025 and US$4 billion in 2030 (EIC). These are projections, not recorded figures.

foreign.note: EIC calls pharmaceutical manufacturing a government priority; check licensing with the regulator.

sectors.name: Mining
sectors.tagline: Gold, industrial minerals and construction inputs, plus import substitution.

claims.t: Gold export earnings said to have reached US$672 million in 2021, up 25-fold in two years (EIC).
Ethiopia is said to spend over US$8 billion a year importing coal, iron, fertiliser, marble and granite, chlor-alkali products, ceramics and petroleum (EIC).
Fertiliser imports cost US$688 million, 5% of total imports (EIC).
National cement demand estimated at 17 million tonnes a year against 8.8 million tonnes of local production (EIC).
EIC's 2030 mining projections (14% of GDP, 37% of export earnings) are targets, not forecasts.

opportunities: Construction inputs: cement, ceramics, marble, granite, gypsum, limestone

foreign.note: Mining licences are issued under separate mining law; check with the Ministry of Mines and EIC.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.tagline: Power for a large unserved population and for export to neighbours.

claims.t: About 55% of 116 million people are said to live without electricity; installed capacity 4,478 MW (2021) with a plan to reach 19,900 MW by 2030 (EIC).
Geothermal: power purchase agreements for Corbetti and Tulu Moye signed March 2020, about US$1.2 billion of investment (EIC).
Solar: Metahara (100 MW, Enel) and two ACWA Power projects (250 MW, about US$300 million), all signed in 2019 (EIC).
EIC puts GERD's expected output at 6,450 MW; this dashboard's infrastructure record cites 5,150 MW (Tractebel). The figures differ; check the operator.
EIC aims to more than double electricity exports from 2,803 GWh to 7,184 GWh by 2030, a target. Reported 2024/25 export earnings are on this dashboard.

foreign.note: New generation is developed through PPPs and IPPs per EIC; terms are set in each agreement.

sectors.name: ICT & digital
sectors.tagline: Software, outsourcing and data centres on low-cost power.

claims.t: A 200-hectare ICT park in Addis Ababa is described as plug-and-play (EIC).
Red Fox's data centre, built at a reported US$130 million, went live in 2022; Safaricom Ethiopia began building its own that year (EIC).
The 'Digital Ethiopia 2025' strategy was launched in 2020 (EIC).

foreign.note: Telecom services are licensed separately (see Telecom).

claims.t: Nine UNESCO World Heritage sites, described as the most in Africa (EIC).
Over 800,000 tourist arrivals a year (EIC; the year is not stated, so verify current figures).
Government-launched destination projects at Gorgora, Wonchi and Koisha are open to investors (EIC).

foreign.note: Confirm with EIC and the Ministry of Tourism.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.tagline: An under-served market for hospitals, diagnostics and specialist care.

claims.t: 0.3 hospital beds per 1,000 people; 364 hospitals, of which 17% private and 85% of private hospitals in Addis Ababa (EIC).
More than 6,000 patients a year are said to travel abroad for treatment, spending over US$120 million (EIC).
Healthcare spending projected at US$5 billion by 2024/25 (EIC projection).

foreign.note: Confirm sector rules with EIC and the Ministry of Health.

sectors.name: Transport & logistics
sectors.tagline: Dry ports, logistics cities, rail freight and services on the Djibouti corridor.

claims.t: The sector is said to have been closed to foreign investment until a 2020 investment law opened it (EIC).
Named projects: Modjo Green Logistics Cities, an Indode logistics hub, dry ports at Semera, Dire Dawa, Woreta, Mekelle, Kombolcha and Jijiga (EIC).
Rail links offered for PPP discussion: Ayisha–Berbera (310 km), Modjo–Moyale / LAPSSET (976 km), and a 1,400 km line to Sudan (EIC). This dashboard's corridor records show their status and sources.
Annual import-export trade is described as more than US$20 billion (EIC).

opportunities: Rail-freight handling on the Addis–Djibouti line

foreign.note: EIC states the sector was opened to foreign investors by the 2020 investment law.

sectors.name: Telecom
sectors.tagline: A liberalised market: one private operator launched, a third licence and a part-sale of Ethio Telecom.

claims.t: Safaricom Telecommunications Ethiopia (consortium of Safaricom, Vodafone, Vodacom, CDC Group and Sumitomo) won a 15-year licence in May 2021 with an upfront fee of US$850 million; services launched October 2022 (EIC).

EIC said a third operator licence was being sought (request for proposals, 2023) and a 40% stake in Ethio Telecom was being prepared for sale. Ethio Telecom has since listed on the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (26 May 2026, ESX record on this dashboard); the details of any stake sale are not in these sources.

foreign.note: The telecom sector was opened to competition by a 2018 government decision (EIC).

sectors.name: Financial services
sectors.tagline: Banking opened to foreign competition; capital market launched.

claims.t: EIC says a bill approved in the last quarter of 2022 opened banking to foreign investors, who may establish banks or partner with existing ones.
ESX lists eight companies, seven of them financial (banks and an insurer), per its listed-companies page.

foreign.note: Opened to foreign investors from late 2022 per EIC; licensing is by the National Bank of Ethiopia. Verify current licence conditions.

sectors.name: Privatisation of state enterprises
sectors.tagline: Partial or full sale of state-owned enterprises.

claims.t: EIC says the government is offering to sell state enterprises, in whole or part, including state monopolies in airline, logistics, telecom and energy, and businesses in sugar, tourism and hospitality, and cement expected to be privatised in the short term.
No specific current offers, prices or deadlines are published on that page. Ask EIC or Ethiopian Investments Holding for the live list.

opportunities: Partial stakes in utilities and logistics

foreign.note: Each sale sets its own terms.

summary.text: 16 built; over 300 companies operating in them; EIC invites PPP development of further parks.
Six privately developed parks serving over 200 companies.
Three parks: Burie (Amhara), Yirgalem (Sidama), Bulbula (Oromia), each with a nearby rural transformation centre.

agroTerms: Water at US$0.57 per m³ per month, 12,000 m³ a day
Ready-made sheds of 1,500, 2,500 and 3,500 m² at US$1.5 per m² per month for foreign investors
Land for building at US$1.2 per m² per year
Incentives listed: income-tax exemption, loss carry-over, export tax exemption, customs-duty exemption, franco valuta, export credit guarantee
parks.note: Prices and tariffs are EIC's stated rates on its 2023 pages; confirm current rates before committing. The Special Economic Zone Proclamation No. 1322/2024 (below) may have changed the framework.

items.label: Minimum capital, wholly foreign-owned
items.value: US$200,000 (US$100,000 for architectural or engineering works, technical consultancy, technical testing and analysis, or publishing)

items.label: Minimum capital, joint venture with a domestic partner
items.value: US$150,000 (US$50,000 for the same technical categories)

items.label: Time to an investment permit
items.value: A minimum of 5 days; EIC says about 5 hours if all requirements are met

items.label: Renewal
items.value: Annually at the end of the fiscal year (July)

items.label: Labour cost (EIC claim)
items.value: US$40–135 a month; no statutory minimum wage; wages negotiated

steps: Collect information and requirements from EIC
Prepare company documents (memorandum and articles) and choose a company name
Authenticate foreign documents through a notary, the Ethiopian embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Open a foreign-currency account at the National Bank of Ethiopia with an EIC letter
Deposit the investment capital and get the bank's credit advice
Get a tax identification number (needs an authenticated lease)
Collect the investment permit and commercial registration
